podcast.body: This classic song contains the line, "It's got a backbeat, you can't lose it," which is the only line that actually talks about what the music is. His guitar style is considered to be basically the whole of his technique, with melody lines comparable to Pete Johnson's right-hand piano phrasing. "It's got a backbeat, you can't lose it."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs
srcs.episode: Episode 2: "Roll Em Pete" by Big Joe Turner

podcast.body: This record marked the beginning of a three-single run that cemented Berry's status as rock and roll's premier mythologiser. Having previously sung about "these rhythm and blues" in May 1956, Berry explicitly used the music's new name in this song, propelling him back into the top 10. "Just let me hear some of that rock and roll music. That put him back in the top 10 and everything seemed to be going wonderfully for him."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs
